title: Thin Air
teaches: coasting — an engine you have switched off is not costing you anything
brief:
Halcyon's atmosphere gives out at seventy kilometres. Get above it, and arrive with at least 2 tonnes still in the tanks.

You could hold the engine lit the whole way up. It would work, and it would cost you nearly everything you have. A ship on a ballistic arc is still climbing with the engine off — so burn until the *apoapsis* is where you want it, then stop and let go.
hints: APO is where you *will* end up, not where you are. Burn until it reads high enough and you have already won; the rest is falling upward.
Burning all the way up to 75 km leaves 0.8 t in the tanks. Burning to a 78 km apoapsis and coasting leaves 2.2 t. Same altitude.
The Q sensor reads dynamic pressure. Watching it teaches you where the air actually hurts.

reference.solution:
; Thin Air — burn until the apoapsis clears the air, then stop and coast.
        THROTTLE 1
        BURN    UNTIL APO > 78000
        HALT
